summary: retry_case()'s isolated single-case retry preserved --allow-running-no-tests (it survives _cmd_without_test_specs, which only strips Catch2 tag-filter specs, not option flags) into shard D's cmd. Catch2 ORs a literal comma inside a positional name spec into multiple sub-filters, so a comma-containing case name (real in-repo example: test_software_deployment_store.cpp:1375, 'migrate_from_sqlite fails closed on a legacy file missing ONLY software_packages, with real deployment data in the other two tables') zero-matches both halves; with the flag present that zero-match exits 0 instead of Catch2's default exit 2/4, so retry_case() would report a genuinely-still-failing case as recovered without it ever running. Empirically reproduced against the real binary (exit 2 without the flag, exit 0 with it, both on the identical 'No tests ran' outcome) by the original reporter and independently re-reproduced by 4 downstream reviewers (a verification fork, build-ci's Gate 8 re-review, compliance-officer, and sre) -- all told about the finding as context (so counted as corroboration, not fresh discovery, per this ledger's own echo-vs-independent convention), but each executed their own fresh repro rather than accepting the claim. compliance-officer additionally verified via known-flaky.json history (empty at every point between the flag's introduction on 2026-08-16 via #3169 and this fix, both in this worktree and on origin/dev) that the false-positive path was live but never actually triggered in production CI -- the defect was real and exploitable but had a zero-incident window. A related, narrower residual gap was identified and deliberately left unfixed: Catch2 cannot match a literal-comma (or e.g. embedded '[0]') case name via an unescaped positional spec at all, independent of --allow-running-no-tests, so post-fix such cases in ANY shard always report 'not recovered' (fail-safe) rather than being genuinely retryable-and-recoverable by name. This is a separate, pre-existing, repo-wide limitation (~1029 case names with a comma exist across the whole suite) predating both PR #3169 and this branch, with a fail-safe (never masks, only over-blocks) failure mode -- re-derived by the verification fork as its own LOW-severity, non-blocking item, not actioned in this commit. [disposition context: commit b84cea87f]
trigger: a comma-containing test case name, tagged into pg shard D, later listed in tests/known-flaky.json, that genuinely fails again
classification_rationale: isolated single-case retry surgery did not account for an option flag surviving into a context (single-case, must-match-exactly) where its zero-match tolerance is never legitimate

summary: CI-CAPACITY-01: pulled the real failed CI run (31970369905, Linux gcc-15 debug, self-hosted Big Tam) that timed out shard C's OLD 1149-case content at 600.57s/600s (SIGKILLed, so 600.57s is a floor not the true completion time). Measured the same content locally (185.3s) and the new post-fix 1083-case content locally (179.8s) -- only a 3.0% local reduction. Scaling that reduction onto the real CI figure projects the new shard C at roughly 97% of its 600s budget on the same contended pool, an optimistic projection since the true local-to-CI contention multiplier is a floor (>=3.24x) not the true value. This diff's routing decision is still correct and necessary (it removes this PR's own marginal load from an already near-ceiling shard) but does not, on this evidence, establish that shard C is safely clear of the ceiling on the pool that actually failed -- no post-fix CI run exists yet (commits unpushed at review time). summary: CI-OBS-01: post-fix, retry_case() correctly returns 'not recovered' for a zero-match on a comma-named case, but it keys only on returncode and discards the run's own output, so the retry report can't distinguish 'ran and genuinely failed N times' from 'never matched a case at all, exit 2, No tests ran'. An operator debugging a shard-D red on a comma-named case gets no hint the retry never executed the case. [disposition context: not yet filed as a GitHub issue, pending operator go-ahead]

summary: CI-ROLLBACK-01: tested both partial-revert directions with git revert --no-commit. Reverting b84cea87f alone (keep the shard-D routing, drop the false-green fix) applies cleanly and passes selftest, but silently re-arms the SHARD-003 defect with no automated check catching that regression (the selftest only exercises the fix's new behavior when present, so its absence is invisible to it). Reverting 070bb326a alone (keep the fix, drop the routing) is safe and coherent. The two commits are therefore asymmetric for partial rollback. [disposition context: recorded here for visibility; no code action taken -- if this PR is ever partially reverted, only 070bb326a should be dropped in isolation, never b84cea87f]
